title.narrative: Capacity building and awareness creation of law enforcement officers on safety of Journalists, freedom of expression and the right to information in Uganda

description.narrative: Media Workers and Law enforcement agencies are often faced with many challenges to balance the rights to freedom of expression with the imperative to maintain impartiality and public order management. During turbulent times, law enforcement agencies have had to manage public safety issues around elections, natural disasters and public health emergencies, and facilitate respect for freedom of expression and the right to peaceful assembly. Political, social and economic circumstances have increasingly encouraged unrest among the public, placing officers in often difficult situations. Against this backdrop, journalists and their freedom are increasingly threathened. A total of 1,088 journalsist have been killed for their work or while on job within the last 12 years. In the first half of 2022 alone, 45 media professionals have been killed. In response, government and law enforcement agencies have had to examine their ways of dealing with public order issues, working with journalists and communicating effectively with the public. Despite the fact that media in Uganda has tremendously expanded and that Uganda’s 1995 constitution, the Press and Journalist Act, 1995 and other existing laws guarantee press freedom, so little has been done to promote media rights, safety and improvement of the working climate and conditions . The threats to free expression and access to information still remain in place. Together with the growing influence of business interests on the media, the threats continue to pose major challenges to the campaign for open dialogue, democratic rights and good governance in Uganda. Concerns of this nature continue to keep human rights defenders in the country on their toes in search for ways to protect and promote open spaces where divergent ideas can flourish to foster democracy. The Ugandan constitution and other existing laws guarantee press freedom, but the state actors usually ignores them at will. To compound the problem, the rate of impunity for crimes against journalists, media workers and social media producers remains high. Those involved in harassing media are never investigated and prosecuted. It is upon this background that we need as a country to promote press freedom at all level so that the gains realized is not washed away by the State actors.
